resources.string: Blinded

You can\'t see. All normal terrain is difficult terrain to you. You can\'t detect anything using vision. You automatically critically fail Perception checks that require you to be able to see, and if vision is your only precise sense, you take a –4 status penalty to Perception checks. You are immune to visual effects. Blinded overrides dazzled.
Clumsy
You take a status penalty equal to the condition value to Dexterity-based rolls and DCs, including AC, Reflex saves, ranged attack rolls, and skill checks using Acrobatics, Stealth, and Thievery.
Confused

You are off-guard (–2 circumstance penalty to AC), don\'t treat anyone as your ally, and can\'t Delay, Ready, or use reactions. Use all your actions to Strike or cast offensive cantrips; the GM determines your targets randomly. With no other viable target you target yourself, automatically hitting but not scoring a critical hit. If you can\'t attack or cast spells, you babble incoherently, wasting your actions. Each time you take damage from an attack or spell, you can attempt a DC 11 flat check to end the condition.
Controlled

Your controller dictates how you act and can make you use any of your actions, including attacks, reactions, or even Delay. The controller usually doesn\'t have to spend their own actions when controlling you.
Dazzled

If vision is your only precise sense, all creatures and objects are concealed from you (DC 5 flat check when targeting them with an attack, spell, or other effect; area effects aren\'t subject to this flat check).
Deafened

You automatically critically fail Perception checks that require hearing. You take a –2 status penalty to Perception checks for initiative and checks that involve sound but also rely on other senses. If you perform an action with the auditory trait, you must succeed at a DC 5 flat check or the action is lost. You are immune to auditory effects while deafened.
Drained

You take a status penalty equal to your drained value on Constitution-based rolls and DCs, such as Fortitude saves. You lose Hit Points equal to your level (minimum 1) times the drained value, and your maximum Hit Points are reduced by the same amount. Each time you get a full night\'s rest, your drained value decreases by 1, but you don\'t immediately recover the lost Hit Points.
Encumbered

You\'re clumsy 1 (–1 status penalty to Dexterity-based rolls and DCs, including AC, Reflex saves, ranged attack rolls, and Acrobatics, Stealth, and Thievery checks) and take a 10-foot penalty to all your Speeds (to a minimum of 5 feet).
Enfeebled
You take a status penalty equal to the condition value to Strength-based rolls and DCs, including Strength-based melee attack rolls, Strength-based damage rolls, and Athletics checks.
Fascinated

You take a –2 status penalty to Perception and skill checks, and you can\'t use concentrate actions unless they (or their intended consequences) are related to the subject of your fascination. This condition ends if a creature uses hostile actions against you or any of your allies.
Fatigued
You take a –1 status penalty to AC and saving throws. You can\'t use exploration activities performed while traveling. You recover from fatigue after a full night\'s rest.
Fleeing
On your turn, you must spend each of your actions trying to escape the source of the fleeing condition as expediently as possible. You can\'t Delay or Ready while fleeing.
Frightened
You take a status penalty equal to the value to all your checks and DCs. Unless specified otherwise, at the end of each of your turns, the value decreases by 1.
Grabbed

You\'re off-guard (–2 circumstance penalty to AC) and immobilized (you can\'t use actions with the move trait). If you attempt a manipulate action while grabbed, you must succeed at a DC 5 flat check or it is lost.
Immobilized

You can\'t use any actions that have the move trait. If something holds you in place and an external force would move you out of your space, the force must succeed at a check against either the DC of the effect holding you in place or the relevant defense (usually Fortitude DC) of the monster holding you.
Off-Guard

You take a –2 circumstance penalty to AC. Some effects make you off-guard only to certain creatures or against certain attacks; if a rule doesn\'t say so, it applies to everything. (Called flat-footed before the remaster.)
Paralyzed

You\'re off-guard (–2 circumstance penalty to AC) and can\'t act except to Recall Knowledge and use actions that require only your mind. Your senses still function, but only in the areas you can perceive without moving, so you can\'t Seek.
Petrified

You can\'t act, nor can you sense anything. You become an object with double your normal Bulk (typically 12 if Medium or 6 if Small), AC 9, Hardness 8, and the same current Hit Points you had when alive. If the statue is destroyed, you immediately die.
Prone

You\'re off-guard (–2 circumstance penalty to AC) and take a –2 circumstance penalty to attack rolls. The only move actions you can use are Crawl and Stand; standing up ends the condition. You can Take Cover while prone to gain greater cover against ranged attacks (+4 circumstance bonus to AC against them), but you remain off-guard.
Quickened

You gain 1 additional action at the start of your turn each round. Many effects that make you quickened limit how you can use this extra action. Because quickened has its effect at the start of your turn, you don\'t immediately gain actions if you become quickened during your turn.
Restrained
You\'re tied up or pinned. You\'re off-guard and immobilized, and you can\'t use any attack or manipulate actions except to attempt to Escape or Force Open your bonds. Restrained overrides grabbed.
Sickened

You take a status penalty equal to the value on all your checks and DCs. You can\'t willingly ingest anything, including elixirs and potions. You can spend a single action retching to attempt a Fortitude save against the DC of the effect; on a success, reduce the value by 1 (2 on a critical success).
Slowed
When you regain your actions at the start of your turn, reduce the number of actions regained by your slowed value. You don\'t immediately lose actions if you become slowed during your turn.
Stunned

You can\'t act. The stunned value is how many total actions you lose. Each time you regain actions, reduce the number you regain by your stunned value, then reduce your stunned value by the number of actions you lost. If stunned has a duration instead, you lose all your actions for the duration. Stunned overrides slowed; actions lost to stunned count toward those lost to slowed.
Stupefied

You take a status penalty equal to the value on Intelligence-, Wisdom-, and Charisma-based rolls and DCs, including Will saves, spell attack modifiers, spell DCs, and skill checks that use these attributes. When you Cast a Spell, it\'s disrupted unless you succeed at a flat check (DC = 5 + value).
Unconscious

You can\'t act. You take a –4 status penalty to AC, Perception, and Reflex saves, and you\'re blinded and off-guard. When you gain this condition, you fall prone and drop items you\'re holding unless the effect states otherwise or the GM determines you\'re positioned so you wouldn\'t.
